source_metadata.title: Dapagliflozin Monotherapy in Type 2 Diabetic Patients With Inadequate Glycemic Control by Diet and Exercise: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated the efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin monotherapy in treatment-naive patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We evaluated the efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin in treatment-naive patients with type 2 diabetes.

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were treatment-naive adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with diet and exercise; enrollment occurred at 85 sites in the United States, Canada, Mexico, and Russia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Men and women with type 2 diabetes, aged 18–77 years, were enrolled between September 2007 and July 2008 at 85 sites in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Russia.

population.label: Treatment-naive adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise

atoms.canonical_statement: Entry criteria included BMI <=45 kg/m2 and fasting C-peptide >=1.0 ng/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Entry criteria included BMI ≤45 kg/m2 and fasting C-peptide ≥1.0 ng/ml.

population.label: Trial eligibility

atoms.canonical_statement: Key exclusions included type 1 diabetes, substantial renal impairment by sex-specific creatinine thresholds, UACR >200 mg/mmol, marked liver enzyme elevation, recent cardiovascular events including NYHA III/IV heart failure, and severe uncontrolled hypertension.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were excluded if they had a history of type 1 diabetes, serum creatinine ≥133 μmol/l (men) or ≥124 μmol/l (women), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio >200 mg/mmol ... a cardiovascular event ... within 6 months ... and severe uncontrolled blood pressure.

population.label: Trial eligibility
exclusion_criteria: Serum creatinine >=133 μmol/L in men or >=124 μmol/L in women
AST or ALT >3 times upper limit of normal
Cardiovascular event including NYHA class III/IV heart failure within 6 months
Systolic BP >=180 mmHg and/or diastolic BP >=110 mmHg

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial was a 24-week randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study with a placebo lead-in.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a 24-week randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial with a 2-week diet/exercise placebo lead-in.

atoms.canonical_statement: Main-cohort participants received dapagliflozin 2.5 mg orally once daily in the morning for 24 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with A1C 7.0–10% were randomly assigned equally ... to receive once-daily placebo or 2.5, 5, or 10 mg dapagliflozin ... in the morning (main cohort).

atoms.canonical_statement: Main-cohort participants received dapagliflozin 5 mg orally once daily in the morning for 24 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with A1C 7.0–10% were randomly assigned equally ... to receive once-daily placebo or 2.5, 5, or 10 mg dapagliflozin ... in the morning (main cohort).

atoms.canonical_statement: Main-cohort participants received dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily in the morning for 24 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with A1C 7.0–10% were randomly assigned equally ... to receive once-daily placebo or 2.5, 5, or 10 mg dapagliflozin ... in the morning (main cohort).

atoms.canonical_statement: The main morning-dose cohort used once-daily placebo for 24 weeks as the control.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with A1C 7.0–10% were randomly assigned equally to one of seven arms to receive once-daily placebo or 2.5, 5, or 10 mg dapagliflozin.

atoms.canonical_statement: Exploratory evening-dose cohorts received dapagliflozin 2.5, 5, or 10 mg once daily in the evening for 24 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with A1C 7.0–10% were randomly assigned equally ... to receive ... dapagliflozin, administered once daily either in the morning (main cohort) or evening (exploratory cohort) for 24 weeks.

atoms.canonical_statement: The exploratory high-A1C cohort was randomized 1:1 to blinded dapagliflozin 5 mg or 10 mg once daily in the morning, without placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with A1C 10.1–12% (high-A1C exploratory cohort) were assigned randomly in a 1:1 ratio to receive blinded treatment with a morning dose of 5 or 10 mg/day dapagliflozin (a placebo group was not included because of the high A1C levels).

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary efficacy endpoint was change from baseline in A1C at week 24 in the main cohort.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary efficacy end point was change from baseline in A1C at week 24 in the main patient cohort.

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary efficacy measures were change from baseline at week 24 in fasting plasma glucose and body weight.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary efficacy measures included change from baseline at week 24 in FPG and body weight.

concept.text: Change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose

atoms.canonical_statement: Body-weight change from baseline at week 24 was a secondary efficacy measure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary efficacy measures included change from baseline at week 24 in FPG and body weight.

concept.text: Change from baseline in body weight

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients meeting prespecified hyperglycemia thresholds could receive open-label metformin rescue; efficacy data obtained after rescue were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with fasting plasma glucose (FPG) >270 mg/dl at week 4, >240 mg/dl at week 8, or >200 mg/dl at weeks 12–24 were eligible for open-label rescue medication (500 mg metformin, titrated as needed up to 2,000 mg).

atoms.canonical_statement: A1C, FPG, and body-weight changes were analyzed by ANCOVA with treatment group as effect and baseline value as covariate; point estimates and 95% confidence intervals were calculated.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Analyses of change from baseline in A1C, FPG, and body weight were performed using an ANCOVA with treatment group as effect and baseline value as covariate. Point estimates and 95% CI were calculated.

atoms.canonical_statement: For the principal week-24 efficacy table, A1C, FPG, and body-weight analyses used last observation carried forward among patients with baseline and postbaseline data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Assessed in patients without missing baseline and week 24 values with last observation carried forward.

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety assessments included adverse events, vital signs, laboratory measurements, and prospective monitoring for signs or symptoms suggestive of urinary tract and genital infections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Safety assessments included vital signs, laboratory measurements, and adverse events ... patients were actively monitored for clinical signs and symptoms suggestive of urinary tract infections (UTIs) and genital infections.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the main morning-dose cohort, 274 participants were randomized to placebo (75), dapagliflozin 2.5 mg (65), 5 mg (64), or 10 mg (70); 232 completed the study.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Placebo n=75; 2.5 mg n=65; 5 mg n=64; 10 mg n=70; completed 63, 60, 52, and 57, respectively.

population.label: Main morning-dose cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: At week 24, morning dapagliflozin 2.5 mg produced a mean A1C change of -0.58 percentage points from baseline in the main cohort; placebo changed by -0.23 percentage points.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Week 24 A1C change: placebo −0.23%; dapagliflozin 2.5 mg -0.58%.

atoms.canonical_statement: The investigators reported no clinically relevant changes in renal-function parameters, including serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, or cystatin C, with dapagliflozin treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There were no clinically relevant changes in any renal function parameter including serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, or cystatin C.

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean seated systolic and diastolic blood pressure decreased in dapagliflozin arms without a notable increase in orthostatic hypotension, and rates of hypotension/dehydration/hypovolemia were reported as similar across placebo and dapagliflozin arms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A decrease in mean seated blood pressure with no notable increase in orthostatic hypotension was observed in the dapagliflozin arms. Rates of hypotension/dehydration/hypovolemia were similar among placebo and dapagliflozin arms.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the main morning-dose cohort, reported hypoglycemia occurred in 2.9% (2/70) with dapagliflozin 10 mg and 2.7% (2/75) with placebo; no event was major and none caused discontinuation.

atoms.canonical_statement: One death occurred in the dapagliflozin 10 mg group and was attributed to a motor vehicle accident.

atoms.canonical_statement: Across pooled morning and evening cohorts, greater fractional renal glucose excretion was associated with greater body-weight reduction at week 24 (r = -0.13, P = 0.008).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: changes from baseline in fractional renal glucose excretion at week 24 were significantly related (r = −0.13, P = 0.008) with the corresponding changes in body weight.

population.label: Pooled morning and evening dapagliflozin/placebo cohorts

concept.text: Association between fractional renal glucose excretion and body-weight change

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that dapagliflozin monotherapy produced clinically meaningful reductions in A1C and FPG in treatment-naive type 2 diabetes, with favorable effects on weight, blood pressure, and other metabolic parameters.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Administration of dapagliflozin as monotherapy to treatment-naive patients with type 2 diabetes resulted in clinically meaningful decreases in A1C and FPG, along with favorable effects on weight, blood pressure, and other metabolic parameters.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors noted that the body-weight difference versus placebo was not statistically significant, that a large placebo effect from diet/exercise counseling may have attenuated the apparent weight effect, and that longer-term studies were needed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although the decrease in body weight in our study did not reach statistical significance compared with placebo ... long-term studies are needed to more precisely gauge the effect of dapagliflozin on weight in the monotherapy setting.
